analysis.title: NVIDIA Corporation: SEC Scrutiny Enhances Risk, but Valuation Provides a Cushion
key_insights: BofA maintains Buy on NVDA with a $280 PO versus a $125.53 price after media reports of an SEC investigation into accounting practices. No details are public on the practices, transactions or periods under review, so BofA calls conclusions on scope or financial impact premature.
The SEC probe adds to a delayed Form 10-Q and a CEO transition, on top of already fragile investor confidence.
BofA estimates neocloud/emerging customers at ~25-30% of sales and direct/indirect China demand at another ~10-15%, together ~40-45% of revenue. Scrutiny is not the same as revenue impairment.
Stress test: if 25-50% of that exposed revenue slowed, NVDA would still earn $10-11 pro forma EPS versus BofA's $15 NTM estimate. That is ~13x PE versus ~30x historically.
Revenue mix over the last twelve months was hyperscalers ~54% and AI cloud/enterprise/industrial ~39%, with neoclouds a meaningful part of the latter.

Direct China Data Center revenue was under 2% last quarter and is effectively zero in BofA forecasts. About 30% of revenue ships overseas and perhaps half could be accessed by China-based users, giving ~15% combined exposure. INTC, AMD, AVGO and QCOM have similar exposure.

As of FQ3'27 NVDA disclosed ~$32bn of neocloud agreements across FY28-32 (<1% of cumulative revenue, BofA est.) and ~$3.5bn of land/power/shell guarantees. These become operative only when counterparties secure financing and capacity is deployed.

NVDA disclosed ~$105bn of credit support tied to land and power development in Ohio, available across customers. Headline commitments should not be treated as financed revenue or losses, though counterparty risk and the financing-to-demand linkage warrant examination.

Exhibit 1 totals ~$407bn of NVDA capital commitments to partners: ~$85bn equity, ~$27bn license/hire, ~$170bn signed backstops and ~$295bn backstops including MOU. This compares with ~$500bn NVDA FCF for CY26-27E.
Exhibit 2 shows $518bn of disclosed future commitments, $32bn additional neocloud commitments and $118bn guarantees as of FQ3'27. Supply and capacity is $390bn of the total.
BofA expects volatility to stay elevated until there is clarity on the SEC inquiry, the 10-Q and CY27 cloud capex plans, likely from early next year.

PO basis is 16x CY27E PE ex cash, within NVDA's historical 15x-56x forward PE range. Downside risks include CEO scrutiny, the SEC probe, competition, China restrictions, lumpy new markets, slower capital returns and antitrust scrutiny.

market_movers.rationale: Valuation cushion holds even if 25-50% of neocloud and China exposed revenue slowed, leaving $10-11 pf-EPS and ~13x PE. SEC probe and 10-Q delay raise uncertainty.

sector_views.rationale: NVDA is rated Buy on leading share in AI compute and networking, with valuation cushioning regulatory risk.

earnings_insights: NVDA Form 10-Q is delayed, with no filing date given in the report.
BofA NTM pro forma EPS estimate is $15 (forecast). A stress case with 25-50% slowing of ~40-45% of revenue gives $10-11 pf-EPS (BofA scenario, not reported).
FQ3'27 disclosures: $518bn future commitments and $118bn guarantees (company-reported).

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA equity, Buy with $280 PO
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuation cushion with ~13x PE in a stress scenario versus ~30x historically.
trade_ideas.risk: SEC probe scope, delayed 10-Q, CEO transition, neocloud counterparty and China exposure.

risk_factors: SEC investigation into accounting practices could affect reported sales and financial statements.
Delayed 10-Q and CEO transition add uncertainty.
Neocloud counterparty risk and financing arrangements tied to GPU demand.
Larger than expected impact from China restrictions.
Competition from public firms, internal cloud projects and private companies.
Lumpy sales in enterprise, data center and autos.
Antitrust scrutiny of NVDA's dominant AI chip position.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 lists NVDA equity, backstop and license/hire commitments to ecosystem partners, totaling ~$407bn versus ~$500bn CY26-27E FCF.
Exhibit 2 tabulates $518bn future commitments by fiscal year, $32bn neocloud commitments and $118bn guarantees as of FQ3'27.
vol_and_positioning: BofA expects NVDA volatility to stay elevated until the SEC inquiry, the 10-Q and CY27 cloud capex plans are clarified, likely from early next year.
NVDA at $125.53 is near the bottom of its 52-week range of $124.50-$243.37.
geopolitical: US export controls (BIS) restrict compute shipments to China, and China retains indirect access via cloud infrastructure legally operated outside the US.
Ongoing US government scrutiny around the NVIDIA CEO is cited as a downside risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Scrutiny is not revenue impairment. Even with 25-50% of neocloud and China exposed revenue slowing, NVDA earns $10-11 pf-EPS, ~13x PE versus ~30x historically.
tension_points.bear_case: The SEC probe, delayed 10-Q and CEO transition compound uncertainty. Neocloud financing structures and China exposure could face revenue recognition and counterparty scrutiny.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disclosure that the SEC probe affects reported sales or financial statements, or neocloud commitments turning into losses, would undermine the valuation cushion.

theme_stances.key_argument: Scrutiny is not equivalent to revenue impairment and valuation cushions downside even in a stressed scenario.
theme_stances.evidence: scrutiny is not equivalent to revenue impairment
